public_payload.normalized_proposition: Salesforce spent millions marketing an AI product that does not exist as sold.

statement.excerpt: Salesforce, one of the most-prominent hypesters behind the AI bubble has spent millions of dollars on advertising and marketing to promote a product that doesn’t exist in the way that it’s being sold.

from_speaker: spent millions of dollars on advertising and marketing
a product that doesn’t exist in the way that it’s being sold
our_interpretation: The product is Agentforce, identified by the surrounding discussion of customer demonstrations.
Read 'millions' as at least two million US dollars spent on Agentforce promotion cumulatively by publication.
Read the capability allegation as a material mismatch between demonstrated current customer functionality and actual availability. It does not assert that every Agentforce feature is nonexistent.
The spending period has no stated beginning. Availability is assessed as of publication.
The surrounding Bloomberg attribution supplies a reporting context, but no accounting basis is identified for the spending assertion itself.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records establish the stated Agentforce-specific promotional spending and show that material capabilities represented as deployed or presently available were not available as represented.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish spending below the threshold, or establish that the disputed capabilities were available as represented. Clearly disclosed future demonstrations would not establish the alleged mismatch.
